land.text: Britain, retaken in 296 by Constantius Chlorus's subordinate Julius Asclepiodotus after the landing near Southampton Water

successors.note: Northern Gaul had already gone back in 293; the roman-empire dossier's 296 gain restores Britain.

capitals.name: Londinium (London)
capitals.note: Inferred, not stated: none of the three pages opened names a capital; the Carausius page lists three mints for his coinage (Londinium, Rotomagus and possibly Colchester). Londinium is the first-named mint and the chief city of Roman Britain.

rulers.name: Carausius
rulers.title: usurper emperor
rulers.note: Infobox 'Reign: 286-293'; the page has him 'declaring himself Emperor' in 'late 286 or early 287'; assassinated by his finance minister Allectus.

rulers.name: Allectus
rulers.title: usurper emperor
rulers.note: Infobox 'Reign: 293-296'; 'Allectus assassinated Carausius and assumed command himself'; killed in the battle against Constantius's forces in 296.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no row for the Britannic Empire (its Roman Empire shapes 283-286 and 287-298 keep Britain; the roman-empire dossier flags the loss). The Gallic part is the Channel coast around Boulogne plus the Rouen area, a reading of 'northern Gaul'. Neither page gives an area.

correction.text: Britain only: 'In 293 Constantius Chlorus retook Carausius's Gallic territory' and besieged Bononia (Boulogne)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: after the loss of the Gallic territory in 293 the rebel empire is Britain. The Allectus page still calls him 'usurper in Britain and northern Gaul from 293 to 296' and says coin finds suggest 'the recapture of Bononia did not spell the end of the rebel empire', so a foothold on the continent after 293 is possible; the Carausian Revolt page says Constantius retook the Gallic territory in 293 and nothing of 294-295, so Britain only is drawn.

ledger.note: 286: Carausius declares himself emperor in Britain and northern Gaul. 'who usurped power in 286, during the Carausian Revolt, declaring himself emperor in Britain and northern Gaul'; 'In late 286 or early 287 Carausius learned of this sentence and responded by declaring himself Emperor' (the sentence of death ordered by Maximian). The Carausian Revolt page gives 286-296 and says his forces were 'the three legions stationed in Britain', his fleet and a legion seized in Gaul.

region.text: northern Gaul: the Channel coast around Bononia (Boulogne-sur-Mer), Carausius's original naval command, and Rotomagus (Rouen), a mint of his coinage; the pages give no list of the Gallic ports held

ledger.note: 293: Constantius Chlorus retakes the Gallic territory. 'In 293, Constantius Chlorus retook Carausius's Gallic territory, then besieged Bononia (Boulogne)' and built a mole across the harbour mouth; the Carausius page: Constantius 'marched into Gaul and reclaimed it for the empire' and 'isolated Carausius by besieging the port of Gesoriacum (Boulogne-sur-Mer)'. The page names Boulogne, not the rest of the territory, so the region is the researcher's reading.

293: Allectus assassinates Carausius and takes command; the state continues under the same name and land. Allectus page: 'Allectus assassinated Carausius and assumed command himself', infobox 'Reign: 293-296'; the Carausius page's infobox has Carausius dying in 293 and the Allectus page dates the crisis to 293. Neither page gives a month.

region.text: the landing of Asclepiodotus 'near Southampton Water, where they burnt their ships'

ledger.note: September 296: Constantius's invasion lands. 'Constantius launched an invasion to depose him in September 296'; '[Asclepiodotus] landed near Southampton Water, where they burnt their ships'. The page dates the launch to September, not the landing.

region.text: Allectus's defeat in the field, in the Wessex area (Silchester is the archaeological suggestion)

ledger.note: 296: Allectus is killed in battle. 'Allectus himself was killed in the battle'; archaeology suggests 'Calleva Atrebatum (Silchester) or the area surrounding the town was the site of his defeat'. The page names no battle and gives no month; the surviving Franks were massacred at Londinium.

region.text: Britain, whose rebel ruler was killed and whose capital Londinium saw Allectus's remaining men 'massacred'

ledger.note: 296: Britain returns to the Roman Empire after ten years. Carausian Revolt page: 'In 296, Constantius and Asclepiodotus retook Britain'; Allectus page: 'caught up with the remnants of Allectus's men, mostly Franks, at Londinium (London) and massacred them' (no year given for the massacre).

wars.outcome: Roman victory: Constantius retook the Gallic territory and Boulogne in 293, Carausius was assassinated by Allectus in 293, and Constantius and Asclepiodotus retook Britain in 296, Allectus being killed in battle.
wars.note: Carausius page: 'Maximian prepared an invasion of Britain in 288 or 289 to oust him'; the pages opened give no outcome of that preparation and no year for the recognition of Carausius by Maximian and Diocletian on his coinage ('Carausius minted coins and acknowledged and honoured Maximian, and later Diocletian').

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary: Britain is a province-wide reading ('suggests he controlled all of Roman Britain') and the Gallic coast is a reading of 'northern Gaul'.

notes: A rebel state Cliopatria lacks, written because the roman-empire dossier's 286 loss and 296 gain name 'Britannic Empire (Carausius and Allectus)' as counterpart. Three pages opened. No page gives a capital, an area or the Gallic ports held: the capital Londinium is inferred from the mint list, the Gallic region is the Pas-de-Calais plus Seine-Maritime departments (Boulogne and Rouen), and 'Britain' is the gazetteer's Roman Britain region (which includes southern Scotland, Cliopatria's 283-298 Roman Empire shapes reach 55.4 N). Whether Carausius lost all of northern Gaul in 293 is uncertain: the Allectus page keeps 'Britain and northern Gaul from 293 to 296'. The Roman Britain page ('short-lived Britannic Empire from 286 to 296') was not opened. Wikidata id unknown (Wikidata unreachable). Gazetteer: 'Boulogne-sur-Mer' and 'Silchester' (Calleva Atrebatum) are not place names in the gazetteer; Pas-de-Calais and Seine-Maritime stand in for the coast.
